propositions: nested pytest child invoked from tests/_store_isolation.py omits --basetemp and joins pytest user-global numbered temp root, causing session-finish cleanup to synchronously scan and delete unrelated stale trees that exceed the 90-second child timeout after test completes

pytest session finish cleanup through rm_rf and maybe_delete_a_numbered_dir can consume entire child timeout budget when shared numbered root contains thousands of stale entries, despite child test completing and reporting 100%
private --basetemp passed to nested pytest child pointing to caller-owned tmp_path/nested-pytest isolates cleanup scope and prevents shared-root deletion work from starving the child timeout
A/B comparison with 400,000 poisoned shared entries showed cleanup cost of 10.8s (shared root) versus 0.882s (private basetemp), proving cleanup overhead scales with retained entries
